body:
hollow-test mutates source files IN PLACE, and every restore path is process-local. A run killed mid-trial therefore strands a live mutant as an unstaged edit, and the next run refuses with `commit or stash first` — which reads as if the USER's uncommitted work is in the way. The reflex is to commit it, and that is how a mutant ships.

Observed twice: a 10-minute agent tool timeout stranded `? 130 :` flipped to `? 131 :` in a plugin CLI, and an `authorized = false` -> `true` flip was stranded the same way earlier.

## What to build

An on-disk record — the file, its ORIGINAL bytes and the MUTANT bytes — written before each mutation and consumed by the NEXT run, which restores before the dirty-tree check instead of blaming the operator for the dirt. This is the layer that survives a kill nothing can catch. Every write to a source file — the mutation, the per-trial restore and the recovery — is atomic, so a kill mid-write cannot leave bytes matching neither the original nor the mutant, which recovery could only treat as an unresolvable conflict.

Recovery must be provable rather than presumed, because a recovery that guesses is worse than none:

- Restore ONLY when the file is byte-identical to the recorded mutant. Restoring merely because it differs from the original would overwrite whatever the developer did to that file after the crash.
- Ownership is tri-state: only a definite ESRCH authorises recovery.
- The recorded path is repo-relative and re-derived against the repo root, with containment checked against REAL paths so a symlink at any component cannot direct the write outside the checkout.
- Writes are ATOMIC (temp file plus rename), so a process killed mid-write never leaves a truncated file, and they preserve the target's mode. Durability against POWER LOSS is explicitly not claimed and not implemented: the failure modes in scope — SIGKILL, an OOM kill, a tool or CI timeout — kill the process, not the page cache, so the kernel still writes those bytes. fsync would only defend against power loss or a kernel panic, which is not what strands mutants.
- A record that cannot be written fails the run closed.

## Out of scope, deliberately

Handling SIGTERM/SIGHUP. Registering a handler SUPPRESSES the default termination, and the trial loop is synchronous over `spawnSync`, so the handler cannot be dispatched until every remaining mutant has run — measured at 24.6 seconds from SIGTERM to exit on an 8-mutant run. Adding those handlers here would make cancellation WORSE, not better. Making it work needs an asynchronous runner, process-group termination and a run lock; that work is preserved on `wip/hollow-test-cancellation` with its own cross-model review findings, for its own ticket and PR.

The `adlc` dispatcher's failure to forward signals to the tool child is a third, separate defect with its own PR.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A mutant stranded by SIGKILL is restored by the next run and reported via a `recovered` field in `--json`, instead of the dirty-tree refusal.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "recovered by the next run" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
2. A file the developer edited after the crash is NOT overwritten, and the record is kept because it holds the only copy of the original bytes.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "refuses to overwrite work" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
3. The record is written inside the git dir, is invisible to `git status`, and a run that finishes normally removes it.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "in-flight record" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
4. Ownership is tri-state: only a definite ESRCH authorises recovery, EPERM counts as alive, any other probe error is unknown; the probe uses signal 0 and never delivers a real signal.
   Verify: `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/inflight.test.mjs` exits 0.
5. A restore target reached through a symlink at ANY path component, or resolving outside the repository, is refused.
   Verify: covered by the `resolveTarget` case; `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/inflight.test.mjs` exits 0.
6. An atomic write preserves the mode of the file it replaces, so recovering an executable does not clear its executable bit; a failed write leaves no temp file behind, and temps from a dead run are swept while a live run's are left alone.
   Verify: `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/inflight.test.mjs` exits 0.
7. A record that cannot be written fails the run closed rather than mutating unprotected.
   Verify: covered by the `writeRecord THROWS` case; `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/inflight.test.mjs` exits 0.
8. No surviving mutants in the changed code.
   Verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 14` exits 0.
9. No regression across the suite.
   Verify: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0.

Rails are deliberately empty. This ticket exists to change `packages/hollow-test/`, and `rail-freeze` unions rails across every incomplete ticket — declaring a rail on the files it must edit would freeze them for every PR in the repo, including this one.
title: hollow-test must recover a mutant stranded by an interrupted run
